276213069_0480b48f.text: There are at least 2 genetically distinguishable subtypes of tuberoinfundibular A12 neurons: those expressing the dopamine transporter (DAT) and the prolactin receptor (PRLR) (18). Traditionally, A12 neurons express tyrosine hydroxylase (TH), which catalyzes the conversion of l-tyrosine to l-DOPA, and aromatic amino acid decarboxylase (AADC), which converts l-DOPA to dopamine. However, these neurons lack dopamine beta hydroxylase, the enzyme required to convert dopamine to norepinephrine, a feature shared by all central dopaminergic neurons. Developmentally, the DA phenotype in A12 neurons emerges early, and these neurons are among the first hypothalamic neurons to express TH and AADC (4)

276213069_161ba639.text: This review highlights the diverse origins, mechanisms, and physiological roles of tuberoinfundibular dopaminergic A12 neurons in the arcuate nucleus and median eminence, emphasizing their essential role in prolactin regulation and broader influences on growth hormone, metabolism, and hypothalamic development.
